module pe (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [31:0] a,
    input [31:0] b,
    output reg [31:0] c
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
    
    if(rst) begin
        
        c <= 32'b0;
    end else begin
        
        c <= c + (a * b);
    end
end
endmodule

    <description>Edge detector for detecting rising and falling edges of a 1-bit input signal 'a'.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>

        // Sequential logic block triggered on the positive edge of the clock or negative edge of reset
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                // On reset, initialize the previous value of 'a' to 0
                prev_a <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                // Update the previous value of 'a' with the current value of 'a'
                prev_a <= a;
            end
        end
        
        // Combinational logic to detect rising and falling edges
        assign rise = (prev_a == 1'b0 && a == 1'b1);
        assign down = (prev_a == 1'b1 && a == 1'b0);
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="signal_generator">
    <description>Triangle Wave Signal Generator</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <output id="wave" width_description="[4:0]">Generated waveform signal.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="0">Initial state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="1">Incrementing state.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="state" width_description="[1:0]">Register to store the current state.</reg>
        <reg id="wave" width_description="[4:0]">Register to store the generated waveform.</reg>
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on positive edge of clk or negative edge of rst_n
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                // Reset condition: set state to 0 and wave to 0
                state <= 0;
                wave <= 0;
            end else begin
                // State machine to generate triangle wave pattern
                case(state)
                    0: begin
                        // Increment wave value by 1
                        wave <= wave + 1;
                        
                        // Check if wave has reached maximum value (31)
                        if(wave == 31) begin
                            // Transition to next state (incrementing state)
                            state <= 1;
                        end
                    end
                    
                    1: begin
                        // Decrement wave value by 1
                        wave <= wave - 1;
                        
                        // Check if wave has reached minimum value (0)
                        if(wave == 0) begin
                            // Transition back to initial state
                            state <= 0;
                        end
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>Generates a triangular waveform by incrementing and decrementing the wave signal.</implementation>
</module>

    <description>Parallel to serial converter, converts every 4 bits of parallel input to 1 bit of serial output (MSB to LSB).</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>

        <output id="dout">Serial output representing the converted data.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>Assigns the most significant bit of the parallel input to the serial output (dout). On each clock cycle, if the counter (cnt) is 3, indicating the last bit of the parallel input, the module updates the data register (data) with the parallel input (d), resets the counter (cnt) to 0, and sets the valid signal (valid) to 1. Otherwise, the module increments the counter (cnt) by 1, sets the valid signal (valid) to 0, and shifts the data register (data) one bit to the left, with the most significant bit shifted to the least significant bit. Counter Register: If the reset signal (rst_n) is high, the register (cnt) is incremented by 1.</implementation>
</module>

module fsm #(
    parameter s0 = 3'b000,
    parameter s1 = 3'b001,
    parameter s2 = 3'b010,
    parameter s3 = 3'b011,
    parameter s4 = 3'b100,
    parameter s5 = 3'b101
) (
    input IN,
    output reg MATCH,
    input CLK,
    input RST
);


reg [2:0] ST_cr;

always @(posedge CLK or posedge RST) begin
    if (RST) begin
        ST_cr <= s0;
    end else begin
        case (ST_cr)
            s0: begin
                if (IN == 1'b1) begin
                    ST_cr <= s1;
                end else begin
                    ST_cr <= s0;
                end
            end
            s1: begin
                if (IN == 1'b1) begin
                    ST_cr <= s1;
                end else begin
                    ST_cr <= s2;
                end
            end
            s2: begin
                if (IN == 1'b1) begin
                    ST_cr <= s1;
                end else begin
                    ST_cr <= s3;
                end
            end
            s3: begin
                if (IN == 1'b1) begin
                    ST_cr <= s4;
                end else begin
                    ST_cr <= s0;
                end
            end
            s4: begin
                if (IN == 1'b1) begin
                    ST_cr <= s5;
                end else begin
                    ST_cr <= s2;
                end
            end
            s5: begin
                if (IN == 1'b1) begin
                    ST_cr <= s1;
                end else begin
                    ST_cr <= s2;
                end
            end
            default: ST_cr <= s0;
        endcase
    end
end

always @(*) begin
    if (RST) begin
        MATCH = 1'b0;
    end else if (ST_cr == s4 && IN == 1'b1) begin
        MATCH = 1'b1;
    end else begin
        MATCH = 1'b0;
    end
end

<module id="fsm">
    <description>Mealy FSM detection circuit that detects a single-bit input IN. When the input is 10011, output MATCH is 1, and MATCH is 0 in other cases. Support for continuous input and loop detection.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="IN">Input signal to the FSM.</input>
        <input id="CLK">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="RST">Reset signal to initialize the FSM.</input>
        <output id="MATCH">Output signal indicating a match condition based on the FSM state.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="S0">Initial state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S1">State after detecting '1'.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S2">State after detecting '10'.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S3">State after detecting '100'.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S4">State after detecting '1001'.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S5">State after detecting '10011'.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="current_state" width_description="[2:0]">Register to hold the current state of the FSM.</reg>
        <reg id="next_state" width_description="[2:0]">Register to hold the next state of the FSM.</reg>
        
        // State transition logic
        <always @(posedge CLK or posedge RST)>
            if (RST) begin
                current_state <= S0;
            end else begin
                current_state <= next_state;
            end
        </always>
        
        // Next state logic
        <always @(*) begin
            case(current_state)
                S0: begin
                    if(IN == 1'b1) begin
                        next_state = S1;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = S0;
                    end
                end
                
                S1: begin
                    if(IN == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = S2;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = S1;
                    end
                end
                
                S2: begin
                    if(IN == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = S3;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = S1;
                    end
                end
                
                S3: begin
                    if(IN == 1'b1) begin
                        next_state = S4;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = S0;
                    end
                end
                
                S4: begin
                    if(IN == 1'b1) begin
                        next_state = S5;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = S0;
                    end
                end
                
                S5: begin
                    if(IN == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = S2;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = S1;
                    end
                end
                
                default: next_state = S0;
            endcase
        end
        
        // Output logic
        <assign MATCH = (current_state == S5 && IN == 1'b1) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0;
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>Mealy FSM detection circuit that detects a single-bit input IN. When the input is 10011, output MATCH is 1, and MATCH is 0 in other cases. Support for continuous input and loop detection.</implementation>

<module id="multi_pipe_4bit">
    <description>4-bit unsigned number pipeline multiplier with two levels of registers.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[3:0]">Multiplicand input signal.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[3:0]">Multiplier input signal.</input>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[7:0]">Product output signal.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="size">Number of bits for the multiplier and multiplicand.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <assign id="mul_a_ext" value="'{size{1'b0}}' + mul_a"/> <!-- Extend multiplicand with zeros -->
        <assign id="mul_b_ext" value="'{size{1'b0}}' + mul_b"/> <!-- Extend multiplier with zeros -->
        
        <genvar i;
            for(i = 0; i < size; i=i+1) begin : gen_partial_products
                <assign id="partial_product[i]" value="(mul_b_ext[i]) ? (mul_a_ext << i) : 'd0'/> <!-- Generate partial products based on multiplier bits -->
            end
        end
        
        <reg id="register[0][0]" width_description="[7:0]"/> <!-- Register for storing partial products -->
        <reg id="register[0][1]" width_description="[7:0]"/>
        <reg id="register[0][2]" width_description="[7:0]"/>
        <reg id="register[0][3]" width_description="[7:0]"/>
        
        <reg id="register[1][0]" width_description="[7:0]"/> <!-- Register for storing sums of partial products -->
        <reg id="register[1][1]" width_description="[7:0]"/>
        <reg id="register[1][2]" width_description="[7:0]"/>
        <reg id="register[1][3]" width_description="[7:0]"/>
        
        <always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if(!rst_n) begin
                register[0][0] <= 8'd0; // Reset first level register
                register[0][1] <= 8'd0;
                register[0][2] <= 8'd0;
                register[0][3] <= 8'd0;
                
                register[1][0] <= 8'd0; // Reset second level register
                register[1][1] <= 8'd0;
                register[1][2] <= 8'd0;
                register[1][3] <= 8'd0;
            end else begin
                register[0][0] <= partial_product[0]; // Store partial products in first level register
                register[0][1] <= partial_product[1];
                register[0][2] <= partial_product[2];
                register[0][3] <= partial_product[3];
                
                register[1][0] <= register[0][0] + register[0][1]; // Add partial products in second level register
                register[1][1] <= register[0][2] + register[0][3];
                register[1][2] <= 8'd0;
                register[1][3] <= 8'd0;
            end
        end
        
        <always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if(!rst_n) begin
                mul_out <= 8'd0; // Reset product output
            end else begin
                mul_out <= register[1][0] + register[1][1]; // Calculate final product
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>Extends inputs, generates partial products, stores them in registers, adds them, and outputs the final product.</implementation>

    <description>A multi-bit MUX-based synchronizer. Data remains constant during the period when data_en is high, and data_en is high for at least 3 clk_b clock cycles. When the value of data_en is high, data can be synchronized. The data change frequency of data_in is very low. The change interval between two adjacent data is at least 10 clk_b clock cycles.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk_a">Clock signal A used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="clk_b">Clock signal B used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="arstn">Active-low reset signal A. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="brstn">Active-low reset signal B. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="data_in" width_description="[3:0]">Input data signal of size 4 bits.</input>
        <input id="data_en">Input enable signal that controls the selection operation.</input>
        <output id="dataout" width_description="[3:0]">Output data signal of size 4 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Data Register
        reg [3:0] data_reg;
        always @(posedge clk_a or negedge arstn) begin
            if (~arstn) begin
                data_reg <= 4'd0;
            end else begin
                data_reg <= data_in;
            end
        end
        
        // Enable Data Register
        reg en_data_reg;
        always @(posedge clk_a or negedge arstn) begin
            if (~arstn) begin
                en_data_reg <= 1'd0;
            end else begin
                en_data_reg <= data_en;
            end
        end
        
        // Enable Control Registers
        reg en_clap_one;
        reg en_clap_two;
        
        always @(posedge clk_b or negedge brstn) begin
            if (~brstn) begin
                en_clap_one <= 1'd0;
                en_clap_two <= 1'd0;
            end else begin
                en_clap_one <= en_data_reg;
                en_clap_two <= en_clap_one;
            end
        end
        
        // Output Assignment
        reg [3:0] dataout;
        always @(posedge clk_b or negedge brstn) begin
            if (~brstn) begin
                dataout <= 4'd0;
            end else begin
                if (en_clap_two) begin
                    dataout <= data_reg;
                end else begin
                    dataout <= dataout;
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

    <description>Implement an unsigned 16-bit multiplier using shift and accumulate operations.</description>

        <input id="clk">Chip clock signal.</input>

        <signal id="breg" type="reg" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the multiplier (b).</signal>

        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                // Reset the shift count register to 0
                i <= 0;
            end else if (start && i < 17) begin
                // Increment the shift count register by 1
                i <= i + 1;
            end else begin
                // Reset the shift count register to 0
                i <= 0;
            end
        end
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the rising edge of the clock or the negative edge of the reset signal
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                // Set the multiplication completion flag to 0
                done_r <= 0;
            end else if (i == 16) begin
                // Set the multiplication completion flag to 1
                done_r <= 1;
            end else if (i == 17) begin
                // Reset the multiplication completion flag to 0
                done_r <= 0;
            end
        end
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the rising edge of the clock or the negative edge of the reset signal
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin

                areg <= 0;

                // Initialize the product output register to 0
                yout_r <= 0;

                        // Store the multiplicand (a) in the multiplicand register
                        areg <= ain;
                        // Store the multiplier (b) in the multiplier register
                        breg <= bin;

                    if(cnt == 8'd0)begin

        Otherwise, res_valid is set to res_valid.

<module id="serial2parallel">
    <description>Serial-Parallel Converter</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="din_serial">Serial input data.</input>
        <input id="din_valid">Validity signal for input data.</input>
        <output id="dout_parallel" width_description="[7:0]">Parallel output data (8 bits wide).</output>
        <output id="dout_valid">Validity signal for the output data.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Counter to keep track of the number of serial inputs received
        reg [3:0] cnt;
        
        // Register to store the parallel output data
        reg [7:0] dout_parallel_reg;
        
        // Register to store the validity signal for the output data
        reg dout_valid_reg;
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the positive edge of the clock
        always @(posedge clk) begin
            // Synchronous reset
            if (~rst_n) begin
                // Reset the counter to 0
                cnt <= 4'd0;
                
                // Reset the parallel output data register to 0
                dout_parallel_reg <= 8'd0;
                
                // Set the output validity signal to 0
                dout_valid_reg <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                // Check if the input data is valid
                if (din_valid) begin
                    // Shift the parallel output data left by one bit
                    dout_parallel_reg <= {dout_parallel_reg[6:0], din_serial};
                    
                    // Increment the counter
                    cnt <= cnt + 1;
                    
                    // Check if the counter has reached 7 (indicating 8 inputs received)
                    if (cnt == 4'd7) begin
                        // Set the output validity signal to 1
                        dout_valid_reg <= 1'b1;
                        
                        // Reset the counter to 0
                        cnt <= 4'd0;
                    end else begin
                        // Set the output validity signal to 0
                        dout_valid_reg <= 1'b0;
                    end
                end else begin
                    // Set the output validity signal to 0
                    dout_valid_reg <= 1'b0;
                end
            end
        end
        
        // Assign the parallel output data register to the output port
        assign dout_parallel = dout_parallel_reg;
        
        // Assign the output validity signal register to the output port
        assign dout_valid = dout_valid_reg;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="traffic_light">
    <description>A traffic light system with red, yellow, and green indicators, controlled by a pedestrian request button.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="pass_request">Pedestrian request signal.</input>
        <output id="clock" width_description="[7:0]">Internal counter value.</output>
        <output id="red">Red indicator signal.</output>
        <output id="yellow">Yellow indicator signal.</output>
        <output id="green">Green indicator signal.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="idle">State value for idle state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="s1_red">State value for red state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="s2_yellow">State value for yellow state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="s3_green">State value for green state.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt" width_description="[7:0]">Internal counter register.</reg>
        <reg id="state" width_description="[1:0]">Current state register.</reg>
        <reg id="p_red">Previous red signal register.</reg>
        <reg id="p_yellow">Previous yellow signal register.</reg>
        <reg id="p_green">Previous green signal register.</reg>
        
        // State transition logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                state <= idle;
                p_red <= 0;
                p_yellow <= 0;
                p_green <= 0;
            end else begin
                case(state)
                    idle: begin
                        p_red <= 0;
                        p_yellow <= 0;
                        p_green <= 0;
                        state <= s1_red;
                    end
                    s1_red: begin
                        p_red <= 1;
                        p_yellow <= 0;
                        p_green <= 0;
                        if(cnt == 3) begin
                            state <= s3_green;
                        end else begin
                            state <= s1_red;
                        end
                    end
                    s2_yellow: begin
                        p_red <= 0;
                        p_yellow <= 1;
                        p_green <= 0;
                        if(cnt == 3) begin
                            state <= s1_red;
                        end else begin
                            state <= s2_yellow;
                        end
                    end
                    s3_green: begin
                        p_red <= 0;
                        p_yellow <= 0;
                        p_green <= 1;
                        if(cnt == 3) begin
                            state <= s2_yellow;
                        end else begin
                            state <= s3_green;
                        end
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end
        
        // Counter logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if(!rst_n) begin
                cnt <= 10;
            end else begin
                if(pass_request && green) begin
                    cnt <= 10;
                end else if(!green && p_green) begin
                    cnt <= 60;
                end else if(!yellow && p_yellow) begin
                    cnt <= 5;
                end else if(!red && p_red) begin
                    cnt <= 10;
                end else begin
                    cnt <= cnt - 1;
                end
            end
        end
        
        // Output assignment
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if(!rst_n) begin
                red <= 0;
                yellow <= 0;
                green <= 0;
            end else begin
                red <= p_red;
                yellow <= p_yellow;
                green <= p_green;
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
</module>

<module id="pulse_detect">
    <description>Pulse Detection Module</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="data_in">One-bit input signal.</input>
        <output id="data_out">Output signal indicating the presence of pulses.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="INITIAL">Initial state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="WAIT_FOR_ONE">Waiting for '1'.</parameter>
        <parameter id="ONE_DETECTED">'1' detected.</parameter>
        <parameter id="WAIT_FOR_ZERO">Waiting for '0' after detecting '1'.</parameter>
        <parameter id="ZERO_DETECTED">'0' detected after '1'.</parameter>
        <parameter id="PULSE_END">End of pulse.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="state" width_description="[3:0]">State register.</reg>
        <reg id="next_state" width_description="[3:0]">Next state register.</reg>
        <always_comb>
            case(state)
                INITIAL: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b1) begin
                        next_state = WAIT_FOR_ZERO;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = INITIAL;
                    end
                end
                WAIT_FOR_ONE: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b1) begin
                        next_state = ONE_DETECTED;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = INITIAL;
                    end
                end
                ONE_DETECTED: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = ZERO_DETECTED;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = PULSE_END;
                    end
                end
                WAIT_FOR_ZERO: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = ZERO_DETECTED;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = WAIT_FOR_ONE;
                    end
                end
                ZERO_DETECTED: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = PULSE_END;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = WAIT_FOR_ONE;
                    end
                end
                PULSE_END: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = INITIAL;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = WAIT_FOR_ZERO;
                    end
                end
                default: next_state = INITIAL;
            endcase
        </always_comb>
        
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if(~rst_n) begin
                state <= INITIAL;
            end else begin
                state <= next_state;
            end
        end
        
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if(~rst_n) begin
                data_out <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                case(next_state)
                    INITIAL: data_out <= 1'b0;
                    WAIT_FOR_ONE: data_out <= 1'b0;
                    ONE_DETECTED: data_out <= 1'b0;
                    WAIT_FOR_ZERO: data_out <= 1'b0;
                    ZERO_DETECTED: data_out <= 1'b0;
                    PULSE_END: data_out <= 1'b1;
                    default: data_out <= 1'b0;
                endcase
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>Sequential logic for pulse detection based on the state machine.</implementation>
</module>
